## Resumo da Participação Internacional
Ambos os eventos destacaram a diversidade global na indústria cinematográfica. O 82º Golden Globe foi particularmente notável pela vitória de **Fernanda Torres**, primeira atriz brasileira a vencer um Globo de Ouro por atuação principal, e pela indicação histórica de **Karla Sofía Gascón** como a primeira mulher trans a ser indicada para uma categoria principal de filme. Atores internacionais representativos incluem representantes da Itália, Colômbia, Finlândia, Áustria e diversos países europeus e asiáticos nas listas de coadjuvação e atuações principais.

The **81st Golden Globe Awards** was an awards ceremony for [film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_in_film "2023 in film") and [American television productions of 2023](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_in_American_television "2023 in American television"). It was broadcast live on January 7, 2024, from [the Beverly Hilton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Beverly_Hilton "The Beverly Hilton") in [Beverly Hills, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beverly_Hills,_California "Beverly Hills, California"), beginning at 5:00 p.m. [PST](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pacific_Time_Zone "Pacific Time Zone") / 8:00 p.m. [EST](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eastern_Time_Zone "Eastern Time Zone"), on [CBS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CBS "CBS") and streamed on [Paramount+](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paramount+ "Paramount+") in the United States. It was produced by [Dick Clark Productions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dick_Clark_Productions "Dick Clark Productions"), [Ricky Kirshner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ricky_Kirshner "Ricky Kirshner"), and [Glenn Weiss](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glenn_Weiss "Glenn Weiss"); the latter also served as director.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Otterson-1)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Donnelly-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Schneider-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Winners-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Winners_List-7)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-8) This was the first ceremony after Dick Clark Productions and [Eldridge Industries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eldridge_Industries "Eldridge Industries") took full control of the Golden Globes from the [Hollywood Foreign Press Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hollywood_Foreign_Press_Association "Hollywood Foreign Press Association").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Otterson-1) The ceremony was also the first to air live on CBS in the United States since [1982](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/39th_Golden_Globe_Awards "39th Golden Globe Awards").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Otterson-1) Comedian [Jo Koy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jo_Koy "Jo Koy") hosted the ceremony.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Host-2)

The nominees were announced on December 11, 2023. *[Barbie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbie_(film) "Barbie (film)")* and *[Succession](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Succession_(TV_series) "Succession (TV series)")* both tied for the most nominations with nine each, followed by *[Oppenheimer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oppenheimer_(film) "Oppenheimer (film)")*'s eight.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Nominees-9)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Barbenheimer-10)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-11)

The ceremony also featured the debut of two new categories: "[Cinematic and Box Office Achievement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Cinematic_and_Box_Office_Achievement "Golden Globe Award for Cinematic and Box Office Achievement")" and "[Best Performance in Stand-Up Comedy on Television](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Performance_in_Stand-Up_Comedy_on_Television "Golden Globe Award for Best Performance in Stand-Up Comedy on Television")"[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-New_Categories-12)

Additionally, the cultural phenomenon of "[Barbenheimer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbenheimer "Barbenheimer")" received seventeen nominations, winning seven.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Winners-6)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Barbenheimer-10)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-13)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-14)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-15)

## Ceremony information

This was the first Golden Globe Awards ceremony after the [Hollywood Foreign Press Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hollywood_Foreign_Press_Association "Hollywood Foreign Press Association") (HFPA) disbanded in 2023. On June 12, 2023, the HFPA announced that all of its rights and properties related to the Golden Globes were acquired by [Dick Clark Productions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dick_Clark_Productions "Dick Clark Productions") and [Eldridge Industries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eldridge_Industries "Eldridge Industries").[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-16)

On February 21, 2023, the date of the ceremony was announced. It came back on a Sunday night slot after being moved to Tuesday for the previous year.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Donnelly-4) On September 18, 2023, [Glenn Weiss](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glenn_Weiss "Glenn Weiss") and [Ricky Kirshner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ricky_Kirshner "Ricky Kirshner") were announced as its executive producers and showrunners.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Schneider-5) On November 17, 2023, it was announced that [CBS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CBS "CBS") had acquired the broadcast rights to the ceremony, replacing the Golden Globes' long-time U.S. broadcast partner [NBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBC "NBC").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Otterson-1)

The nominations were announced on December 11, 2023, during an event co-hosted by [Cedric the Entertainer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cedric_the_Entertainer "Cedric the Entertainer") and [Wilmer Valderrama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilmer_Valderrama "Wilmer Valderrama"). Most of the categories were revealed during a live-streaming presentation, while ten of the categories were revealed during another segment on *[CBS Mornings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CBS_Mornings "CBS Mornings")*.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Nominees-9)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-17)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-18)

On December 21, comedian and actor [Jo Koy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jo_Koy "Jo Koy") was announced as the host.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Host-2)[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-19)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-20)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-21)[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-22) Before this announcement, it was reported that a source with knowledge of the conversations told [CNN](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CNN "CNN") that at least five A-list comedic actors, including [Chris Rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Rock "Chris Rock") and [Ali Wong](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ali_Wong "Ali Wong"), declined offers to host; the hosts of the podcast *[SmartLess](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SmartLess "SmartLess")* (actors [Will Arnett](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Will_Arnett "Will Arnett"), [Jason Bateman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jason_Bateman "Jason Bateman"), and [Sean Hayes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Hayes "Sean Hayes")) also reportedly declined the offer.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-23) That same month, *[TheWrap](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TheWrap "TheWrap")* reported that 64 voters threatened to withhold their final-round votes in protest, after being told that they would not be given tickets to the ceremony.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-24)

With the awards no longer being overseen by the HFPA, a new, racially and ethnically diverse group of voters consisting of 300 journalists representing 76 countries selected the 2023 nominees and winners.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Winners_List-7)

For her portrayal of [Mollie Burkhart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mollie_Kyle "Mollie Kyle") in *[Killers of the Flower Moon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Killers_of_the_Flower_Moon "Killers of the Flower Moon")*, [Lily Gladstone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lily_Gladstone "Lily Gladstone") became the first [Indigenous](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Native_Americans_in_the_United_States "Native Americans in the United States") actor to win a Golden Globe Award, winning for [Best Actress in a Motion Picture – Drama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Actress_in_a_Motion_Picture_–_Drama "Golden Globe Award for Best Actress in a Motion Picture – Drama").[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-25)

### Expansion

On September 26, 2023, it was announced that two new categories would be added for the upcoming ceremony: "[Cinematic and Box Office Achievement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Cinematic_and_Box_Office_Achievement "Golden Globe Award for Cinematic and Box Office Achievement")" (a category for films that grossed at least $100 million domestically and $150 million worldwide) and "[Best Performance in Stand-Up Comedy on Television](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Performance_in_Stand-Up_Comedy_on_Television "Golden Globe Award for Best Performance in Stand-Up Comedy on Television")" (also known as "Best Stand-Up Comedian on Television").[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-New_Categories-12)[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-26)[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-27)[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-28)[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-29) Some critics felt that the new categories were an attempt to improve the ceremony's viewership and relevance, with comparisons drawn to the [Academy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Awards "Academy Awards")' [attempt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/91st_Academy_Awards#Proposed_"Popular_Film"_category "91st Academy Awards") to introduce a [category for "Popular Film"](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Outstanding_Achievement_in_Popular_Film "Academy Award for Outstanding Achievement in Popular Film") in [2018](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/91st_Academy_Awards "91st Academy Awards").[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-30)[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-31)[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-32)[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-33)

### Reduction

The two Lifetime Achievement Awards (the [Cecil B. DeMille Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Cecil_B._DeMille_Award "Golden Globe Cecil B. DeMille Award") and the [Carol Burnett Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Carol_Burnett_Award "Golden Globe Carol Burnett Award")) were not presented this year, but expected to return in the future. Executive Vice President Tim Gray explained that with the change in ownership and status, and 25 of the competitive categories expanding from 5 nominees to 6, the increase will also include a reduction with no presentation of the two aforementioned awards for this year. "This is not a permanent change, with future awards slated to be given," Gray wrote in a post on the Globes' official website.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-34)

## Reception

### Criticism of Jo Koy's opening monologue

| External videos | |
| --- | --- |
| [![video icon](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/1b/Nuvola_apps_kaboodle.svg/20px-Nuvola_apps_kaboodle.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Nuvola_apps_kaboodle.svg) [Jo Koy Opening Monologue \| 81st Annual Golden Globes](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=KvSHHnucouo) | |
[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/be/Jo_Koy_by_Gage_Skidmore.jpg/250px-Jo_Koy_by_Gage_Skidmore.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Jo_Koy_by_Gage_Skidmore.jpg)[Jo Koy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jo_Koy "Jo Koy"), host of the 81st Golden Globe Awards

Host [Jo Koy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jo_Koy "Jo Koy")'s opening [monologue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monologue "Monologue") was met with criticism from viewers and critics with many describing his jokes as "cringeworthy", "painful", and "unfunny". Chelsey Sanchez of *[Harper's Bazaar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harper's_Bazaar "Harper's Bazaar")* described the monologue as "awkward" and "distasteful".[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-35) Koy was also criticized for putting blame on his writers during the monologue, coming after the lengthy [2023 Writers Guild of America strike](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Writers_Guild_of_America_strike "2023 Writers Guild of America strike"). Justin Curto of *[Vulture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vulture_(website) "Vulture (website)")* noted that when some of his jokes fell flat, Koy "immediately threw his writers under the bus... He yelled. 'Yo, shut up. You're kidding me, right. Slow down. I wrote some of these and they're the ones you're laughing at'".[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-36) Marlow Stern of *[Rolling Stone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rolling_Stone "Rolling Stone")* noted that many of Koy's jokes drew "groans" and "boos" from the audience.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-37)

Among jokes that drew the most ire were those about the film *[Barbie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbie_(film) "Barbie (film)")*, and attending nominees [Robert De Niro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_De_Niro "Robert De Niro"), [Meryl Streep](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meryl_Streep "Meryl Streep") and [Taylor Swift](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift "Taylor Swift"); the latter's reaction went viral.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-38)[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-39)[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-40) Shirley Li of *[The Atlantic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Atlantic "The Atlantic")* wrote: "Practically every joke failed to land, mostly because the punchlines were dated or obvious."[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-41) Nicole Sperling of *[The New York Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_New_York_Times "The New York Times")*, who was in the audience that night, wrote that she had "never seen an audience rebel against an emcee so quickly" and cited a prominent film director describing the monologue as a "disaster".[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-42)

Conversely, four-time [Academy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Awards "Academy Awards") host and comedian [Whoopi Goldberg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Whoopi_Goldberg "Whoopi Goldberg") defended Koy on *[The View](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_View "The View")*, saying: "These hosting gigs are brutal. They're just brutal. If you don't know the room, if you've not been in these rooms before and you're sort of thrust out there, it's hit or miss. Now, I love Jo Koy, he makes me crazy because he's funny. I don't know whether it was the room, I don't know whether it was the jokes, I didn't get to see it. But I do know, that he is as good as it gets when it comes to stand-ups and it is not an easy gig."[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-43) Actor and comedian [Steve Martin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Martin "Steve Martin") also threw his support behind Koy on [Threads](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Threads_(social_network) "Threads (social network)"), writing: "I tip my hat to anyone who steps out on stage to host a live awards show. It's a very difficult job and not for the squeamish. I know because I'm still throwing up from the last time I did it in 2010. So, Congratulations to Jo Koy, who took on the toughest gig in show business, hit, missed, was light on his feet, and now has twenty minutes of new material for his stand up!"[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-44)

Additionally, comedian [Michael Che](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Che "Michael Che") supported Koy by writing that "comedians should boycott hosting award shows" on [Instagram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Instagram "Instagram").[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-45) When questioned about Koy's jokes aimed toward her film *Barbie*, director [Greta Gerwig](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greta_Gerwig "Greta Gerwig") replied that she was not offended.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-46) On *[Watch What Happens Live with Andy Cohen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Watch_What_Happens_Live_with_Andy_Cohen "Watch What Happens Live with Andy Cohen")*, actor and comedian [Kevin Hart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_Hart "Kevin Hart") said he has "no reaction" to the backlash and went on to praise Koy for being a "phenomenal comedian".[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-47) In a [Facebook](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Facebook "Facebook") post by Filipino actor and comedian [Michael V.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_V. "Michael V."), he posted: "I think Jo Koy's Golden Globes jokes are funny, direct, and pretty much self-explanatory. The last thing Jo Koy should be doing is trying to explain it to people who purposely choose NOT to understand and appreciate them."[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-48)

Koy responded to the criticism in an interview with *[Good Morning America](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Good_Morning_America "Good Morning America")*, admitting: "I'd be lying if [I said] it doesn't hurt," but also admitted, "I had fun. You know, it was a moment that I'll always remember. Hosting is just a tough gig. Yes, I'm a stand-up comic, but that hosting position it's a different style. I kind of went in and did the writer's thing. We had ten days to write this monologue. It was a crash course. I feel bad, but I got to still say I loved what I did."[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-49) In his first stand-up set afterward, Koy mocked the Hollywood celebrities, alluding: "Lot a marshmallows, man. They're delicious, but goddamn, they're soft. I just come from a different time. I see the changes that are happening. I get it, but goddamn, can we fucking laugh at ourselves?"[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-50)

The **82nd Golden Globe Awards** was an awards ceremony that honored [excellence in film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_in_film "2024 in film") and [American television productions of 2024](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_in_American_television "2024 in American television"). The winners were revealed during the live telecast, airing on [CBS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CBS "CBS") and streaming on [Paramount+](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paramount+ "Paramount+") on January 5, 2025.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-2) The event was hosted by comedian [Nikki Glaser](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nikki_Glaser "Nikki Glaser"), making her the first solo female host in Golden Globes history.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Glaser-3)

The nominations were announced live on December 9, 2024, at a [press conference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Press_conference "Press conference") at [the Beverly Hilton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Beverly_Hilton "The Beverly Hilton") by actors [Morris Chestnut](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morris_Chestnut "Morris Chestnut") and [Mindy Kaling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mindy_Kaling "Mindy Kaling"), following an introduction from Golden Globes president, Helen Hoenhe.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Globes-4) *[Emilia Pérez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emilia_Pérez "Emilia Pérez")*, with 10 nominations, became the most nominated comedy/musical film in [Golden Globes history](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Awards#Superlatives "Golden Globe Awards"), just 1 shy of the overall record of 11, set by [Robert Altman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Altman "Robert Altman")'s [country music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Country_music "Country music") [satire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Satire_(film_and_television) "Satire (film and television)") *[Nashville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nashville_(film) "Nashville (film)")* in the drama category in [1976](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/33rd_Golden_Globe_Awards "33rd Golden Globe Awards").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-5) *[The Brutalist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brutalist "The Brutalist")* received the second-most in film with 7 nominations, followed by *[Conclave](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conclave_(film) "Conclave (film)")* with 6.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-6) Additionally, *[The Bear](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series) "The Bear (TV series)")* led the television nominations with 5, followed by *[Only Murders in the Building](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Only_Murders_in_the_Building "Only Murders in the Building")* and *[Shōgun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shōgun_(2024_TV_series) "Shōgun (2024 TV series)")* with 4 each.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Variety-7)

## Ceremony information

On August 28, 2024, comedian [Nikki Glaser](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nikki_Glaser "Nikki Glaser") was announced as the host for this year's ceremony, following last year's widely criticized host, comedian [Jo Koy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jo_Koy "Jo Koy").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Glaser-3) She is the first woman to host the Golden Globes solo.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-8) Glaser herself was nominated for [Best Performance in Stand-Up Comedy on Television](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Performance_in_Stand-Up_Comedy_on_Television "Golden Globe Award for Best Performance in Stand-Up Comedy on Television") for her [HBO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HBO "HBO") comedy special, *Nikki Glaser: Someday You'll Die*,[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Governors-9) but lost to [Netflix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netflix "Netflix")'s *Ali Wong: Single Lady*.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-10)

The ceremony was held at 5:00 p.m. [PST](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pacific_Time_Zone "Pacific Time Zone") / 8:00 p.m. [EST](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eastern_Time_Zone "Eastern Time Zone") on January 5, 2025. It was broadcast live on [CBS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CBS "CBS") and streamed on [Paramount+](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paramount+ "Paramount+").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Globes-4) [Glenn Weiss](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glenn_Weiss "Glenn Weiss") and [Ricky Kirshner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ricky_Kirshner "Ricky Kirshner") of White Cherry Entertainment returned from last year to executive produce the ceremony, along with [Dick Clark Productions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dick_Clark_Productions "Dick Clark Productions").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Globes-4)

On December 3, 2024, it was announced that the two Lifetime Achievement Awards, which were not presented last year, would return this year; however, they were presented during an untelevised gala dinner on January 3, 2025, prior to the telecast, similar to the [Academy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Awards "Academy Awards")' [Governors Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Governors_Awards "Governors Awards").[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Governors-9) The recipient of the [Cecil B. DeMille Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Cecil_B._DeMille_Award "Golden Globe Cecil B. DeMille Award") was [Viola Davis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Viola_Davis "Viola Davis"), while the [Carol Burnett Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Carol_Burnett_Award "Golden Globe Carol Burnett Award") was awarded to [Ted Danson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_Danson "Ted Danson").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-11)

*[Emilia Pérez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emilia_Pérez "Emilia Pérez")* star [Karla Sofía Gascón](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karla_Sofía_Gascón "Karla Sofía Gascón") was the first [trans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transgender "Transgender") nominee for a Golden Globe motion picture acting category, for the [Best Actress in a Musical or Comedy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Actress_in_a_Motion_Picture_–_Musical_or_Comedy "Golden Globe Award for Best Actress in a Motion Picture – Musical or Comedy") category.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-12) [Jacques Audiard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jacques_Audiard "Jacques Audiard"), the director and writer of the film, was one of the most nominated individuals, with a total of three nominations: [Best Director](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Director "Golden Globe Award for Best Director"), [Best Screenplay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Screenplay "Golden Globe Award for Best Screenplay"), and co-lyricist of [Best Original Song](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Original_Song "Golden Globe Award for Best Original Song") nominee "[El Mal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/El_Mal_(song) "El Mal (song)")".[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Variety-7) The composers and co-lyricists of the song, [Camille](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Camille_(French_singer) "Camille (French singer)") and [Clément Ducol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clément_Ducol "Clément Ducol"), tied Audiard for most nominated individuals. Aside from "El Mal", they were also jointly nominated for composing *Emilia Pérez*'s [Best Original Score](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Original_Score "Golden Globe Award for Best Original Score") and an additional Best Original Song nominee: "[Mi camino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mi_camino "Mi camino")".[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Variety-7)

This year's nominations were tabulated by [KPMG](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KPMG "KPMG"), the U.S. audit, tax, and advisory firm, taking over [Ernst & Young](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ernst_&_Young "Ernst & Young") after fifty plus years.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Globes-4)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-13)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-14)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-15) [Netflix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netflix "Netflix") received a total of 36 nominations between film and television, the most of any distributor.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-16)

*Emilia Pérez* is the first non-English-language film (with some parts of English in the film) to win [Best Motion Picture – Musical or Comedy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Motion_Picture_–_Musical_or_Comedy "Golden Globe Award for Best Motion Picture – Musical or Comedy"). *[Flow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flow_(2024_film) "Flow (2024 film)")* is the first [Latvian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latvian_language "Latvian language") film to win [Best Animated Feature Film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Animated_Feature_Film "Golden Globe Award for Best Animated Feature Film").[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-17) [Fernanda Torres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fernanda_Torres "Fernanda Torres") became the first [Brazilian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brazilian_Portuguese "Brazilian Portuguese") actress to win a Golden Globe in an acting category,[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Torres-18) as well as the first Brazilian, first [South American](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_America "South America") and first [Portuguese-speaking](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portuguese_language "Portuguese language") actor to win the [Golden Globe Award for Best Actress in a Motion Picture – Drama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Actress_in_a_Motion_Picture_–_Drama "Golden Globe Award for Best Actress in a Motion Picture – Drama").[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Torres-18) She acknowledged her mother [Fernanda Montenegro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fernanda_Montenegro "Fernanda Montenegro")'s nomination, for *[Central Station](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Station_(film) "Central Station (film)")* (1998), in the same category at the [56th Golden Globe Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/56th_Golden_Globe_Awards "56th Golden Globe Awards").[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Torres-18)

*Emilia Pérez* and *[Shōgun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shōgun_(2024_TV_series) "Shōgun (2024 TV series)")* were the biggest winners of the night, for film and television, respectively, with four wins each.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Winners-19) *[The Brutalist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brutalist "The Brutalist")* was the next biggest film recipient, with three wins; for television, *[Baby Reindeer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baby_Reindeer "Baby Reindeer")* and *[Hacks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hacks_(TV_series) "Hacks (TV series)")* each won two.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Winners-19)

pergunta: Can you list for me all the usa secretaries of education from the beginning of 2018 until the end of 2024? including short acting secretaries
resposta:
Here are the U.S. Secretaries of Education from the beginning of 2018 until the end of 2024:

1.  **Betsy DeVos** (November 5, 2017 – January 20, 2021)
    *   Served under President Donald Trump. She was confirmed by the Senate on November 5, 2017, and served until her resignation on January 20, 2021.

2.  **Miguel Cardona** (January 20, 2021 – January 20, 2025)
    *   Served under President Joe Biden. He was confirmed by the Senate on March 1, 2021, and served until his resignation on January 20, 2025.

3.  **Denise Carter** (Acting Secretary, January 20, 2025 – January 20, 2025)
    *   Served as an Acting Secretary for a brief period in early 2025 after Miguel Cardona's resignation. She did not serve during the 2018-2024 timeframe but is included for completeness.

4.  **Linda McMahon** (March 3, 2025 – Present)
    *   Served under President Donald Trump. She was confirmed by the Senate on February 26, 2025, and took office on March 3, 2025. She did not serve during the 2018-2024 timeframe but is included for completeness.

**Summary:**
*   **Betsy DeVos** served from November 5, 2017, to January 20, 2021.
*   **Miguel Cardona** served from January 20, 2021, to January 20, 2025.

There were no short-acting secretaries during the 2018-2024 period. Both secretaries served full terms or until their respective administrations ended.

pergunta: Você pode listar todos os secretários de Saúde e Serviços Humanos dos EUA do início de 2018 até o fim de 2024, incluindo secretários interinos?
resposta:
Com certeza. Abaixo está a lista completa dos Secretários de Saúde e Serviços Humanos (HHS) dos Estados Unidos, do início de 2018 até o fim de 2024, incluindo os secretários interinos (*acting*).

**Período: Janeiro de 2018 a Dezembro de 2024**

Durante este período, houve três administradores presidentiais diferentes (Donald Trump, Joe Biden e Donald Trump novamente).

### **Primeiro Mandato de Donald Trump (2017–2021)**

*   **Alex Azar**
    *   **Cargo:** Secretário Permanente
    *   **Período:** 29 de janeiro de 2018 – 20 de janeiro de 2021
*   *(Intervenção entre a transição de 2020 e 2021)*
    *   **Norris Cochran**
        *   **Cargo:** Secretário Interino
        *   **Período:** 20 de janeiro de 2021 – 19 de março de 2021
    *   **Xavier Becerra**
        *   **Cargo:** Secretário Permanente
        *   **Período:** 19 de março de 2021 – 20 de janeiro de 2025 (inclui o final do mandato de Biden em 2024)

---

### **Mandato de Joe Biden (2021–2025)**

*   **Xavier Becerra** (Continuação do cargo acima)
    *   **Cargo:** Secretário Permanente
    *   **Período:** 19 de março de 2021 – 20 de janeiro de 2025 (inclui todo o período de 2021 a 2024)

---

### **Segundo Mandato de Donald Trump (A partir de 2025)**

*Nota: Este período começa após o fim do mandato de Biden em janeiro de 2025.*

*   **Dorothy Fink**
    *   **Cargo:** Secretária Interina
    *   **Período:** 20 de janeiro de 2025 – 13 de fevereiro de 2025
*   **Robert F. Kennedy Jr.**
    *   **Cargo:** Secretário Permanente
    *   **Período:** 13 de fevereiro de 2025 – Incumbente

---

### **Resumo da Lista (2018-2024)**

1.  **Alex Azar** (Secretário Permanente): Jan 2018 – Jan 2021
2.  **Norris Cochran** (Secretário Interino): Jan 2021 – Mar 2021
3.  **Xavier Becerra** (Secretário Permanente): Mar 2021 – Jan 2025 (Cobriu todo o período restante até 2024)

**Observação importante:** Durante o período de transição em 2020/2021, antes que Becerra fosse nomeado oficialmente, Norris Cochran serviu como secretário interino. Após a eleição de Biden em novembro de 2020, não houve um segundo interino listado para o início do mandato de Biden antes da nomeação oficial de Becerra em março de 2021.

The **United States secretary of health and human services** is the head of the [United States Department of Health and Human Services](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Department_of_Health_and_Human_Services "United States Department of Health and Human Services"), and serves as the principal advisor to the [president of the United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_the_United_States "President of the United States") on health matters. The secretary is a member of the [United States Cabinet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Cabinet "United States Cabinet"). [Robert F. Kennedy Jr.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr. "Robert F. Kennedy Jr.") is the incumbent secretary of health and human services, having held the position since February 13, 2025.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Secretary_of_Health_and_Human_Services#cite_note-2)

The office was formerly known as the secretary of health, education, and welfare. In 1980, the [Department of Health, Education, and Welfare](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Department_of_Health,_Education,_and_Welfare "United States Department of Health, Education, and Welfare") was renamed to Department of Health and Human Services, and its education functions and [Rehabilitation Services Administration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rehabilitation_Services_Administration "Rehabilitation Services Administration") were transferred to the new [United States Department of Education](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Department_of_Education "United States Department of Education").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Secretary_of_Health_and_Human_Services#cite_note-3) [Patricia Roberts Harris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patricia_Roberts_Harris "Patricia Roberts Harris") headed the department before and after it was renamed.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Secretary_of_Health_and_Human_Services#cite_note-4)

Nominations to the office are referred to the [Health, Education, Labor and Pensions Committee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Senate_Committee_on_Health,_Education,_Labor,_and_Pensions "United States Senate Committee on Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions") and the [United States Senate Committee on Finance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Senate_Committee_on_Finance "United States Senate Committee on Finance"), which has jurisdiction over Medicare and Medicaid,[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Secretary_of_Health_and_Human_Services#cite_note-5) before confirmation is considered by the full [United States Senate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Senate "United States Senate"). The secretary of health and human services is a [level I position in the Executive Schedule](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Executive_Schedule#Level_I "Executive Schedule"),[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Secretary_of_Health_and_Human_Services#cite_note-6) thus earning a salary of [US$](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/US_Dollar "US Dollar")250,600, as of January 2025.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Secretary_of_Health_and_Human_Services#cite_note-Salary-7)

## Duties

[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/28/Flag_of_the_Secretary_of_Health%2C_Education%2C_and_Welfare.png/250px-Flag_of_the_Secretary_of_Health%2C_Education%2C_and_Welfare.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Flag_of_the_Secretary_of_Health,_Education,_and_Welfare.png)The flag of the secretary of health, education, and welfare, the predecessor to the current office

The duties of the secretary revolve around human conditions and concerns in the [United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States "United States"). This includes advising the [president](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_the_United_States "President of the United States") on matters of [health](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Health "Health"), [welfare](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Social_security "Social security"), and income security programs. The secretary strives to administer the Department of Health and Human Services to carry out approved programs and make the public aware of the objectives of the department.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Secretary_of_Health_and_Human_Services#cite_note-8)

The [Department of Health, Education and Welfare](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Department_of_Health,_Education,_and_Welfare "United States Department of Health, Education, and Welfare") (HEW) was reorganized into a [Department of Education](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Department_of_Education "United States Department of Education") and a [Department of Health and Human Services](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Department_of_Health_and_Human_Services "United States Department of Health and Human Services") (HHS).

The Department of Health and Human Services oversees 11 agencies including the [Food and Drug Administration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Food_and_Drug_Administration "Food and Drug Administration") (FDA), [Centers for Disease Control](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Centers_for_Disease_Control "Centers for Disease Control") (CDC), [National Institutes of Health](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Institutes_of_Health "National Institutes of Health") (NIH), [Administration for Children and Families](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Administration_for_Children_and_Families "Administration for Children and Families") (ACF) and [Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Centers_for_Medicare_and_Medicaid_Services "Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services") (CMS).[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Secretary_of_Health_and_Human_Services#cite_note-9)

# [2404.08191] Measuring Cross-lingual Transfer in Bytes

[View PDF](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2404.08191) [HTML (experimental)](https://arxiv.org/html/2404.08191v1)
> Abstract:Multilingual pretraining has been a successful solution to the challenges posed by the lack of resources for languages. These models can transfer knowledge to target languages with minimal or no examples. Recent research suggests that monolingual models also have a similar capability, but the mechanisms behind this transfer remain unclear. Some studies have explored factors like language contamination and syntactic similarity. An emerging line of research suggests that the representations learned by language models contain two components: a language-specific and a language-agnostic component. The latter is responsible for transferring a more universal knowledge. However, there is a lack of comprehensive exploration of these properties across diverse target languages. To investigate this hypothesis, we conducted an experiment inspired by the work on the Scaling Laws for Transfer. We measured the amount of data transferred from a source language to a target language and found that models initialized from diverse languages perform similarly to a target language in a cross-lingual setting. This was surprising because the amount of data transferred to 10 diverse target languages, such as Spanish, Korean, and Finnish, was quite similar. We also found evidence that this transfer is not related to language contamination or language proximity, which strengthens the hypothesis that the model also relies on language-agnostic knowledge. Our experiments have opened up new possibilities for measuring how much data represents the language-agnostic representations learned during pretraining.

# Measuring Cross-lingual Transfer in Bytes

---

##### Abstract

Multilingual pretraining has been a successful solution to the challenges posed by the lack of resources for languages. These models can transfer knowledge to target languages with minimal or no examples. Recent research suggests that monolingual models also have a similar capability, but the mechanisms behind this transfer remain unclear. Some studies have explored factors like language contamination and syntactic similarity. An emerging line of research suggests that the representations learned by language models contain two components: a language-specific and a language-agnostic component. The latter is responsible for transferring a more universal knowledge. However, there is a lack of comprehensive exploration of these properties across diverse target languages. To investigate this hypothesis, we conducted an experiment inspired by the work on the Scaling Laws for Transfer. We measured the amount of data transferred from a source language to a target language and found that models initialized from diverse languages perform similarly to a target language in a cross-lingual setting. This was surprising because the amount of data transferred to 10 diverse target languages, such as Spanish, Korean, and Finnish, was quite similar. We also found evidence that this transfer is not related to language contamination or language proximity, which strengthens the hypothesis that the model also relies on language-agnostic knowledge. Our experiments have opened up new possibilities for measuring how much data represents the language-agnostic representations learned during pretraining.

# Secretário de Estado dos Estados Unidos

| Secretário de Estado dos    Estados Unidos | |
| --- | --- |
| *United States Secretary of State* | |
| [![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/fc/Seal_of_the_United_States_Secretary_of_State.svg/120px-Seal_of_the_United_States_Secretary_of_State.svg.png?utm_source=pt.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ficheiro:Seal_of_the_United_States_Secretary_of_State.svg)   Selo do Secretário de Estado | |
| [![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/ee/Flag_of_the_United_States_Secretary_of_State.svg/250px-Flag_of_the_United_States_Secretary_of_State.svg.png?utm_source=pt.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ficheiro:Flag_of_the_United_States_Secretary_of_State.svg)   Bandeira do Secretário de Estado | |
| [![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b7/Official_portrait_of_Secretary_Marco_Rubio%2C_January_2025.jpg/250px-Official_portrait_of_Secretary_Marco_Rubio%2C_January_2025.jpg?utm_source=pt.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ficheiro:Official_Portrait_of_Secretary_Rubio.jpg)   No cargo   [Marco Rubio](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marco_Rubio "Marco Rubio")   desde 21 de janeiro de 2025 | |
| [Departamento de Estado](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Departamento_de_Estado_dos_Estados_Unidos "Departamento de Estado dos Estados Unidos") | |
| Designado por | [Presidente](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidente_dos_Estados_Unidos "Presidente dos Estados Unidos") com [consentimento](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conselho_e_consentimento "Conselho e consentimento") do [Senado](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Senado_dos_Estados_Unidos "Senado dos Estados Unidos") |
| Duração | Não possui mandato específico |
| Criado em | [6 de abril](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/6_de_abril "6 de abril") de [1789](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/1789 "1789") (237 anos) |
| Primeiro titular | [Thomas Jefferson](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thomas_Jefferson "Thomas Jefferson")[[1]](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret%C3%A1rio_de_Estado_dos_Estados_Unidos#cite_note-1) |
| Sucessão | [4º](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Linha_de_sucessão_presidencial_dos_Estados_Unidos_da_América "Linha de sucessão presidencial dos Estados Unidos da América") |
| *Website* | [www.state.gov](https://www.state.gov) |

O **Secretário de Estado dos Estados Unidos** é o título do chefe do [Departamento de Estado dos Estados Unidos](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Departamento_de_Estado_dos_Estados_Unidos "Departamento de Estado dos Estados Unidos"), que lida com os [assuntos externos](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Relações_internacionais "Relações internacionais"), equivalente ao [Ministério dos Negócios Estrangeiros](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ministério_dos_Negócios_Estrangeiros "Ministério dos Negócios Estrangeiros") em Portugal, ao [Ministério das Relações Exteriores](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ministério_das_Relações_Exteriores_(Angola) "Ministério das Relações Exteriores (Angola)") em Angola e ao [Itamaraty](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Itamaraty "Itamaraty") no Brasil. O Secretário é um membro do Gabinete Presidencial e a mais alta classificação de um secretário do gabinete tanto na linha de sucessão quanto na ordem de precedência. O atual secretário de Estado, selecionado pelo [presidente](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidentes_dos_Estados_Unidos_da_América "Presidentes dos Estados Unidos da América") [Donald Trump](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donald_Trump "Donald Trump"), é o ex-senador [Marco Rubio](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marco_Rubio "Marco Rubio").

O cargo de Secretário de Estado é uma das mais altas posições no governo norte-americano. Três dos últimos quatro Secretários de Estado foram mulheres. Dois dos últimos três Secretários de Estado foram [afro-americanos](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Afro-americano "Afro-americano"). Desde a [independência](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Declaração_de_Independência_dos_Estados_Unidos "Declaração de Independência dos Estados Unidos") dos [Estados Unidos](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Estados_Unidos "Estados Unidos") até [1996](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/1996 "1996"), apenas homens brancos representaram seu país como Secretário de Estado; de 2001 em diante, nenhum homem branco assumiu esta posição até Kerry em fevereiro de 2013.

## História

Em [10 de janeiro](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/10_de_janeiro "10 de janeiro") de [1781](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/1781 "1781"), o [Segundo Congresso Continental](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Segundo_Congresso_Continental "Segundo Congresso Continental") criou o Departamento de Assuntos Externos.[[2]](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret%C3%A1rio_de_Estado_dos_Estados_Unidos#cite_note-2) Em [27 de julho](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/27_de_julho "27 de julho") de [1789](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/1789 "1789"), [George Washington](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Washington "George Washington") assinou um projeto de lei congressional reautorizando um Departamento de Assuntos Externos executivo, chefiado pelo Secretário de Assuntos Externos. O Congresso então passou outra lei, dando certas responsabilidades domésticas adicionais ao novo Departamento e mudando seu nome para Departamento do Estado, e o nome do chefe do departamento para Secretário de Estado. Washington aprovou esse ato em [15 de setembro](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/15_de_setembro "15 de setembro") de [1789](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/1789 "1789").

Os novos deveres domésticos atribuídos ao renomeado departamento foram: recebimento, publicação, distribuição, e preservação das leis dos Estados Unidos, sob vigilância do [Grande Selo dos Estados Unidos](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grande_Selo_dos_Estados_Unidos "Grande Selo dos Estados Unidos"); autenticação de cópias e preparação de comissões de nomeações do [poder executivo](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Poder_executivo "Poder executivo"); e, finalmente, custódia dos livros, papéis e recordes do [Congresso Continental](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Congresso_Continental "Congresso Continental"), incluindo a [Constituição dos Estados Unidos](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Constituição_dos_Estados_Unidos "Constituição dos Estados Unidos") e a [Declaração de Independência](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Declaração_de_Independência_dos_Estados_Unidos "Declaração de Independência dos Estados Unidos").

Nos primeiros anos da república, o [Vice-presidente](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vice-presidente_dos_Estados_Unidos "Vice-presidente dos Estados Unidos") seria aquele que tivesse o segundo lugar na quantidade de votos eleitorais, e poderia ter vindo de um partido político diferente do [presidente](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidente_dos_Estados_Unidos "Presidente dos Estados Unidos"). O Secretário de Estado, como membro do mesmo partido político do presidente, foi, muitas vezes, visto como um natural trampolim para a presidência. A gama de Secretários de Estado que, mais tarde, ocuparam a [Casa Branca](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Casa_Branca "Casa Branca"), incluem: [Thomas Jefferson](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thomas_Jefferson "Thomas Jefferson"), [James Madison](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Madison "James Madison"), [James Monroe](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Monroe "James Monroe"), [John Quincy Adams](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Quincy_Adams "John Quincy Adams"), [Martin Van Buren](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martin_Van_Buren "Martin Van Buren") e [James Buchanan](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Buchanan "James Buchanan"). Já a gama de Secretários que, sem êxito, tentaram a presidência (seja antes ou após seu serviço no Departamento de Estado) incluem: [Henry Clay](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Clay "Henry Clay"), [Daniel Webster](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daniel_Webster "Daniel Webster"), [John C. Calhoun](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_C._Calhoun "John C. Calhoun"), [William H. Seward](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_H._Seward "William H. Seward"), [James G. Blaine](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_G._Blaine "James G. Blaine"), [Walter Q. Gresham](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walter_Q._Gresham "Walter Q. Gresham"), [John Sherman](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Sherman "John Sherman"), [Elihu Root](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elihu_Root "Elihu Root"), [William Jennings Bryan](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Jennings_Bryan "William Jennings Bryan"), [Charles Evans Hughes](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_Evans_Hughes "Charles Evans Hughes"), [Edmund Muskie](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edmund_Muskie "Edmund Muskie"), [John Kerry](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Kerry "John Kerry") e [Hillary Rodham Clinton](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hillary_Rodham_Clinton "Hillary Rodham Clinton").

## Funções

[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b4/Letter_of_Resignation_of_Richard_M._Nixon%2C_1974.jpg/250px-Letter_of_Resignation_of_Richard_M._Nixon%2C_1974.jpg?utm_source=pt.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ficheiro:Letter_of_Resignation_of_Richard_M._Nixon,_1974.jpg)Carta de demissão de [Richard Nixon](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon "Richard Nixon") a [Henry Kissinger](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Kissinger "Henry Kissinger").

Muitas das não originais funções domésticas do Departamento de Estado têm sido transferidas para outras agências. Aquelas que permanecem incluem armazenamento e o uso do [Grande Selo dos Estados Unidos](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grande_Selo_dos_Estados_Unidos "Grande Selo dos Estados Unidos"), desempenho das funções do protocolo da [Casa Branca](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Casa_Branca "Casa Branca"), elaboração de discursos, e respostas a inquéritos. De acordo com a [Constituição dos Estados Unidos](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Constituição_dos_Estados_Unidos "Constituição dos Estados Unidos"), o Secretário desempenha funções tais como o presidente exige. Isto inclui negociações com representantes estrangeiros e instrução da [embaixada](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Embaixada "Embaixada") dos [Estados Unidos](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Estados_Unidos "Estados Unidos") ou consulados no exterior. O Secretário também serve como principal conselheiro do presidente, em determinação da política de externa dos Estados Unidos e, nas últimas décadas, tem se tornado responsável pela direção, coordenação e supervisão geral de atividades interdepartamentais do governo estadunidense ultramarino, exceto certas atividades militares. Como o mais alto cargo do gabinete, o Secretário de Estado é o quarto na linha de sucessão da presidência, vindo após o [Vice-presidente](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vice-presidente_dos_Estados_Unidos "Vice-presidente dos Estados Unidos"), o [Presidente da Câmara dos Representantes dos Estados Unidos](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidente_da_Câmara_dos_Representantes_dos_Estados_Unidos "Presidente da Câmara dos Representantes dos Estados Unidos"), e o [Presidente pro tempore do Senado dos Estados Unidos](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidente_pro_tempore_do_Senado_dos_Estados_Unidos "Presidente pro tempore do Senado dos Estados Unidos"). (*Ver: [Linha de sucessão presidencial dos Estados Unidos](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Linha_de_sucessão_presidencial_dos_Estados_Unidos "Linha de sucessão presidencial dos Estados Unidos").*) A lei federal ([3 U.S.C. § 20](http://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/3/20.html)) prevê que uma demissão presidencial deve ser efetuada por comunicação escrita do [presidente](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidente_dos_Estados_Unidos "Presidente dos Estados Unidos") ao escritório do Secretário de Estado. Isto ocorreu apenas uma vez, quando o [presidente](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lista_de_presidentes_dos_Estados_Unidos "Lista de presidentes dos Estados Unidos") [Richard Nixon](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon "Richard Nixon") renunciou em agosto de [1974](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/1974 "1974") via uma carta ao seu Secretário de Estado [Henry Kissinger](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Kissinger "Henry Kissinger").

## Secretário de estado adjunto dos Estados Unidos

[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f2/Deputy_Secretary_Sherman%27s_Official_Photo_%2851142275093%29.jpg/250px-Deputy_Secretary_Sherman%27s_Official_Photo_%2851142275093%29.jpg?utm_source=pt.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ficheiro:Deputy_Secretary_Sherman's_Official_Photo_(51142275093).jpg)**[Wendy Sherman](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wendy_Sherman "Wendy Sherman") é** a atual Secretária de Estado Adjunta.

O **Secretário de Estado adjunto** dos Estados Unidos é o principal adjunto do Secretário de Estado. A atual secretária de Estado adjunta é [Wendy Ruth Sherman](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wendy_Sherman "Wendy Sherman"), servindo desde abril de 2021 sob o secretário de Estado [Antony Blinken](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken "Antony Blinken").[[101]](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret%C3%A1rio_de_Estado_dos_Estados_Unidos#cite_note-101) Se o secretário de Estado renunciar ou morrer, o secretário de Estado adjunto torna-se secretário de Estado interino até que o [Presidente](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidente_dos_Estados_Unidos "Presidente dos Estados Unidos") nomeie e o [Senado](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Senado_dos_Estados_Unidos "Senado dos Estados Unidos") confirme um substituto. A posição foi criada em 1972. Antes de 13 de julho de 1972, o Subsecretário de Estado tinha sido o segundo oficial de ranking do [Departamento de Estado](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Departamento_de_Estado_dos_Estados_Unidos "Departamento de Estado dos Estados Unidos"). A posição foi mais recentemente ocupada por Stephen Biegun.

O Departamento de Estado é a única agência federal de nível de gabinete que tinha dois secretários adjuntos co-iguais em sua história. O segundo secretário adjunto de Estado, o Secretário adjunto de Estado de Gestão e Recursos, atuou como "primeiro assistente" para fins da Lei de Reforma das Vagas, mas ambos os secretários adjuntos tinham total autoridade delegada para atuar para o secretário, se não fosse proibido por lei. Eles estão listados com uma designação "B", abaixo, durante os anos do presidente [Barack Obama](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama "Barack Obama"), sob o comando da secretária [Hillary Clinton](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hillary_Clinton "Hillary Clinton") e do secretário [John Kerry](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Kerry "John Kerry"). Esses deputados foram [Jack Lew](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jack_Lew "Jack Lew"), que, após quase dois anos no Departamento de Estado, deixou para se tornar [Chefe de Gabinete](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chefe_de_Gabinete_da_Casa_Branca "Chefe de Gabinete da Casa Branca") de Obama e, em seguida, mais tarde [Secretário do Tesouro](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secretário_do_Tesouro_dos_Estados_Unidos "Secretário do Tesouro dos Estados Unidos") em 2013;[[102]](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret%C3%A1rio_de_Estado_dos_Estados_Unidos#cite_note-102) Thomas Nides, que havia prometido apenas 2 anos de serviço e, posteriormente, retornou para ser o diretor de operações do [Morgan Stanley](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morgan_Stanley "Morgan Stanley");[[103]](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret%C3%A1rio_de_Estado_dos_Estados_Unidos#cite_note-103)[[104]](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret%C3%A1rio_de_Estado_dos_Estados_Unidos#cite_note-104) e Heather Higginbottom, que preencheu o segundo mandato de Barack Obama sob o secretário Kerry como a primeira mulher secretária de Estado adjunta.[[105]](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret%C3%A1rio_de_Estado_dos_Estados_Unidos#cite_note-105)[[106]](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret%C3%A1rio_de_Estado_dos_Estados_Unidos#cite_note-106) Esta prática foi encerrada sob o presidente [Donald Trump](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donald_Trump "Donald Trump").

Alguns secretários de Estado adjuntos foram nomeados secretário de Estado, como [Warren Christopher](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warren_Christopher "Warren Christopher") em 1992[[107]](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret%C3%A1rio_de_Estado_dos_Estados_Unidos#cite_note-107) e [Lawrence Eagleburger](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lawrence_Eagleburger "Lawrence Eagleburger") em 1993 sob o presidente [William Jefferson Clinton](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Clinton "Bill Clinton"),[[108]](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret%C3%A1rio_de_Estado_dos_Estados_Unidos#cite_note-108) e [Antony Blinken](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken "Antony Blinken"), como secretário de Estado sob o presidente [Joseph Biden](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Biden "Joe Biden") em 2021.[[109]](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret%C3%A1rio_de_Estado_dos_Estados_Unidos#cite_note-109)

**Data da Cerimônia:** 5 de janeiro de 2025
**Ano do Evento:** 82º Aniversário dos Prêmios Globo de Ouro

Abaixo está a lista completa de vencedores em todas as categorias, dividida por Cinema e Televisão.

*   **Melhor Filme - Drama:** *The Brutalist*

*   **Realização Cinematográfica e Conquista no Bilheteira:** *Wicked*

## 📺 CATEGORIAS DE TELEVISÃO (TELEVISION)

*   **Melhor Série de Drama:** *Shōgun*

*   **Melhor Série Limitada, Anthologia ou Filme para TV:** *Baby Reindeer*
*   **Melhor Ator em Série Limitada, Anthologia ou Filme para TV:** Colin Farrell (*The Penguin*)
*   **Melhora Atriz em Série Limitada, Anthologia ou Filme para TV:** Jodie Foster (*True Detective: Night Country*)
*   **Melhor Comédia em Stand-Up na Televisão:** Ali Wong (*Single Lady*)

Segundo os dados oficiais da noite, os seguintes títulos se destacaram ao vencer múltiplas categorias:

    *   *Total: 4 prêmios*

    *   Melhor Filme - Drama
    *   Melhor Ator - Drama (Adrien Brody)
    *   Melhor Diretor (Brady Corbet)
    *   *Total: 3 prêmios*

4.  **"Hacks"** (Série de TV)
    *   Melhor Série de Comédia/Musical
    *   Melhor Atriz - Comédia/Musical (Jean Smart)
    *   *Total: 2 prêmios*

5.  **"Baby Reindeer"** (Série de TV)
    *   Melhor Atriz de Apoio (Jessica Gunning)
    *   Melhor Série Limitada/Anthologia/Filme para TV
    *   *Total: 2 prêmios*
